statement: Long-term, intermittent in vivo partial reprogramming in middle-aged mice altered age-associated molecular changes without causing tumours or loss of cell identity over the treatment period.

measurement.assay: transcriptomic and epigenetic age-associated changes; histology
measurement.effect: age-associated changes altered; no tumours reported

evidence.note: epigenetic information loss as a driver, with reprogramming as a partial reversal

replication.note: Two groups (Izpisua Belmonte; Sinclair), both invested in the reprogramming hypothesis.

limitations: molecular endpoints rather than function or lifespan in the wild-type animal

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
